transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I... I guess I came in because I am just so, so tired. And I don't mean just regular tired, you know? It's like... well, I work as a cashier, and usually, standing at the register all day is fine, I've been doing it long enough that I'm used to it. But lately, I can barely get through a single shift. I'll just be standing there at the belt and it feels like my whole body is just... heavy. Like every part of me is filled to the brim with wet sand. My arms, my legs, even just trying to hold my head up to look at the customers, it all just feels bogged down with this thick, heavy, wet sand. 

And you'd think, okay, just go home and get some sleep, right? So I try to do that. I go home, I take my work vest off, I lie down, but resting doesn't really bring me back. I can lie there and try to recharge, but when I get up, the sand is still there. It's dragging me down so much that just scanning a barcode or bagging a few groceries feels like I'm lifting boulders. I just don't understand why I can't shake this exhaustion no matter how much I try to rest, it's just so heavy...
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in your usual activities?

Yeah... yeah, actually, that's exactly what's happening. And it bothers me so much because, well, normally I'm someone who really likes my downtime, you know? Like, after a long week at the register, I usually have my little routines that keep me going. I used to really love cooking for myself. I'd go to the store, pick out fresh ingredients, and spend a whole evening just chopping vegetables and trying out a new recipe. But lately? I just open the fridge and stare at it. The food is right there, but the desire to make anything is just... gone. It all just feels so flat. 

And my guitar, too. I've played since I was in high school, nothing professional, just for me, but usually picking it up and strumming for an hour makes me feel so much better if I've had a rough day. I tried to play a few days ago, I just sat on the edge of my bed, and I couldn't even make it through one song. The music just sounded like noise. I didn't feel anything at all, so I just put it right back in the case. 

Even getting outside... I love hiking. There are these trails not too far from my place that I usually hike almost every weekend, rain or shine, just to get some fresh air. Now I look out the window and I just can't see the point of walking around in the woods. I don't even want to put my boots on. 

But I think the hardest part, honestly, is my family. I went over to my family's place recently, which is usually this big, loud, fun thing for us. And I was sitting there at the dining table, surrounded by everyone laughing and talking, and it was like I wasn't even really in the room. I was just... going through the motions. Smiling when they smiled, nodding when my sister talked about her week, but inside I was completely blank. It felt like I was only pretending to care, like I was an actor playing myself in my own life. I don't know why everything lost its color like that, but nothing gives me that spark anymore. Everything is just flat.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Well, I... I guess I haven't really been keeping track of the exact days, you know? Like, I couldn't tell you if it's been exactly fourteen days or sixteen days or whatever, because the days all just kind of bleed into each other lately. I wake up, and it's just this same heavy feeling, and then I go to work, and it's still there, and then I come home, and it's still there. But as for feeling down or depressed... I don't know if I'd use those exact words. It's more just... empty. 

Like I was saying about the guitar and the hiking, it's not like I'm sitting around crying all day. I'm just... existing. And I guess maybe that is what being depressed is? I don't know. But it's not like a sharp sadness, it's just a dull, flat nothingness. And it's been going on for a while now, definitely a few weeks, maybe more. It's hard to pinpoint when exactly the color started draining out of everything. I just remember waking up one Tuesday—or maybe it was a Wednesday, I had the early shift—and just thinking, "What is the point of any of this?" And that feeling just hasn't left. So, I don't know if that counts as being depressed most of the day, but it definitely feels like a cloud that just won't move.
Would you say that most days, for the past few weeks, you've felt this way—like you're just going through the motions and everything feels flat—pretty much all day long?

Yeah, pretty much all day long, every single day. And it's... it's been going on for a lot longer than just a few weeks, honestly. If I really sit down and trace it back, think about when things really started to shift and get so heavy, this low, empty, flat feeling has been dragging on for about four months now. 

Four whole months. It feels like an eternity when you're stuck inside it, you know? Because I remember exactly what it was like before this started. Back then, there was this period at work where I was just... I don't know, I was flying through my shifts. I had this huge rush of energy, like I could ring up a hundred customers an hour and still have enough gas in the tank to reorganize all the endcaps and clean the breakroom. I felt unstoppable, really. I was talking to everyone, moving so fast, just buzzing. 

But then that passed. That rush just sort of evaporated, and right after that, this... this heaviness set in. And it's just stayed. For four months, ever since that high energy disappeared, I've just been slogging through this empty feeling. It's like someone flipped a switch from fast-forward straight into slow-motion, and the remote is just broken now. I keep waiting to wake up and feel like myself again, or even just feel that buzz I had before, but it's just been day after day, month after month of this same gray, flat nothingness from the minute I wake up until I finally manage to fall asleep.
